dedupe_keys.name: nict space weather forecast regional warning center japan

description: The NICT space weather forecast site, run by the Space Environment Laboratory of the Applied Electromagnetic Research Institute, gives the latest information on the space environment near Earth for people who operate communications and broadcasting infrastructure and space systems. It covers solar flares, protons, solar wind, geomagnetic disturbances, radiation belt electrons, ionospheric storms and sporadic E-layer events, with the current sun, current status charts, predictions and observations. The page says NICT has delivered space environment forecasts and alerts since 1949, began its space weather forecasting project in 1988, has acted as the Regional Warning Center of the International Space Environment Service since 1996, and also provides information on HF communications and GNSS positioning. Access is free online in Japanese and English; the site states all rights reserved and gives no open licence. Caveats: products are forecasts and charts, not a documented download service on the page read. Coverage is global space weather with a focus on Japan. It supports hazard exposure and emergency response planning for space weather effects on communications, GNSS and power systems; related records are the Met Office space weather forecast, Space Weather Canada and the INGV eSWua service.
